speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your specific symptoms regarding the gait and limb ataxia, and list your significant medical history so I can begin my assessment.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance suggests significant ataxia. To narrow this down, on which side is the ataxia more pronounced, and do you have any other significant medical history, particularly regarding past strokes, trauma, or genetic conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.

This diagnosis is highly consistent with your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, a medication known to increase the risk of PML, which presents with subacute gait and limb ataxia. I am requesting MRI images of your brain to confirm the presence of white matter lesions characteristic of PML.
